catalog_quote: Знак ˘ («ташдид»), употребляемый в арабско-персидской графике для обозначения усиления или геминации согласных ..., использовался предположительно также для маркирования места ударения: pnyr 'сыр' — [pánīr]. ... Ударение падало на основу, при этом место словесного ударения, предположительно, могло изменяться в зависимости от двух факторов: 1. new_statements.translation: Stress fell on the stem; the place of word stress could, presumably, change depending on two factors: 1. A word standing before a pause (at the end of a phrase or in isolation) takes a so-called 'pausal' form with a lengthened vowel before the last consonant (...). This is assumed to be the result of a transfer of stress onto that vowel, cf. st'rk 'star', before pause st'ryk (see also 5.1.2). 2. When suffixes, enclitics or the second member of a compound are added to a word, its final vowel after the last consonant was lengthened (...). This change too is connected with a transfer of stress onto that word-final vowel, whereby an initial unstressed vowel, now still further from the stress, could be reduced and lost [cf. uδir 'belly' ~ δər-βánd 'girth'].

new_statements.rule_in_words: Reconstructed for an extinct language written mostly without vowels: stress basically on the stem (MacKenzie 1989: nouns paroxytone or initial-stressed, i.e. near the beginning of the word, as in Ossetic; verbal personal endings unstressed, augment/initial syllable of imperfects and subjunctives mostly stressed); stress shifts rightward (a) onto the last stem vowel in pre-pausal (citation/isolation) forms, which is written plene, and (b) onto the word-final vowel immediately preceding an added pronominal suffix/enclitic or second compound member. The only direct evidence is plene 'pausal' spellings and the shadda sign in a few vowelled MSS, which MacKenzie judges 'to some extent contradictory' and 'inconclusive'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: nothing said in any source read.
new_statements.exceptions: Edelman hedges the whole account with 'предположительно/предполагается'. MacKenzie 1989 lists counter-examples: 2pl imperatives with stressed ending (hiβrífa, packanífa), 2sg forms in pause with final stress (xurī́na), mkn ~ mkñ variation 'inexplicable', imperfects with and without lengthened (stressed) first vowel in equal numbers; monosyllables with shadda may reflect sentence stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Pausal (pre-pause / isolation, i.e. citation-form) shapes differ systematically from sentence-internal shapes, and the stress account is built on that alternation plus enclisis; so the 'word' here is the word-plus-enclitics group, and citation forms are precisely the pausal forms with the rightward-shifted (pre-final-consonant) stress. All evidence is orthographic (13th-14th c. MSS); no living speakers.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Late (Islamic-period) Khwarezmian/Chorasmian, the East Middle Iranian language of Khwarezm attested in Arabo-Persian script c. 11th-14th c. (Muqaddimat al-adab glosses, Qunyat al-munya law-book sentences) = Glottolog khwa1238, ISO xco. Not the Turkic Khorezm dialect of Uzbek. Old/Middle Chorasmian (Aramaic-script coins, Toprak-kala documents) is too fragmentary for any prosodic statement and is not what the quotes describe.

sources.note: sec. 5.1.0, p. 96: stress fell on the stem; its place presumably shifted (1) in pausal position onto the (lengthened) vowel before the last consonant (st'rk ~ pausal st'ryk), (2) before suffixes/enclitics/2nd compound member onto the lengthened word-final vowel (δuγda ~ δuγdā-mi), with reduction/loss of a now-distant initial unstressed vowel (uδir ~ δər-βánd); p. 95: tashdid presumably also marked stress place (pnyr [panīr]); 5.1.2 p. 97 restates pausal lengthening as stress transfer.
